header:
Date: 2025-10-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Ava (Triton Procurement), Marcus (Triton CTO), Priya (Triton Sec), Elliot (Platform PM)
Recording: yes
summary: Intro procurement gate readout; Triton confirms constraints around data residency and KMS; pricing sensitivity discussed with request for pilot economics and an on-prem/VPC fallback; legal asked for MSA redlines timeline; technical team wants a short private deployment ridealong and latency SLOs; next steps: pricing deck, security deep dive, legal redlines exchange.
topics: Pricing for pilot vs committed Dedicated capacity
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:08] Ava (Triton): Ava here, Marcus, Priya, Elliot on.
[00:12] Marcus (Triton): Hey.
[00:14] Leah (Redwood-SE): Leah here, Maya's on as well.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood): Cool. Agenda: procurement gate readout, clarify legal timeline for MSA/DPA, pricing ask for pilot, and short tech preflight for VPC/KMS.
[00:28] Ava (Triton): Sounds good — we have a 2pm internal gate later this week so wanted to surface blockers.
[00:33] Marcus (Triton): From our side main constraints are data residency in EU for customer data, and we need KMS integration with our HSM, also latency under 120ms for inference tail.
[00:45] Leah (Redwood-SE): Got it. we support both hosted and private; Dedicated can give predictable throughput, Private (VPC) lets you bring your KMS. There may be a small variance with quantized models but we can target 90-110ms in most scenarios.
[01:05] Priya (Triton): Quick Q — do you have SOC2 and iso certs? our procurement team needs those to move forward.
[01:12] Maya (Redwood-CSM): Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001, Maya will drop links after the call.
[01:18] Priya (Triton): perfect. also need an audit log sample showing per-token user attribution.
[01:24] Samir (Redwood): We'll include an audit log sample; keep in mind some PII is scrubbed in hosted logs but for Private deployments you control retention.
[01:36] Elliot (Triton): On pricing: procurement is pushing for unit economics comparison — can you put pilot pricing vs monthly committed Dedicated?
[01:44] Samir (Redwood): Absolutely, I'll send a two-slide break down: pilot hourly + per-token estimate versus committed pool pricing and break-even projection.
[01:52] Ava (Triton): Our gate wants clarity on liability and indemnity in the MSA, DPA exceptions ok but need clarity on egress fees.
[02:02] Samir (Redwood): Understood. our standard MSA has an egress section; we can flag it for legal, and propose a cap for the pilot.
[02:12] Marcus (Triton): Also curious about fallback — if Dedicated goes down do you auto-failover to a cheaper model or cross-region? what's the SLA?
[02:20] Leah (Redwood-SE): We have routing policies: failover to a compatible model in the same region, or cross-region fallback, and Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime. For worst-case latency, fallback can add 30-60ms depending on region hop.
[02:36] Speaker 1 (ops): there was a question in the chat about KV cache — is that supported in Private?
[02:42] Leah (Redwood-SE): yes KV cache is supported, though the config differs in on-prem. sometimes transcript tools show "kay vee cache" haha.
[02:50] Priya (Triton): Regarding KMS — we run a cloud HSM (vendor redacted) and would like to bring our key via an external key manager. does Redwood support BYOK and HSM integrations?
[02:59] Leah (Redwood-SE): Yes; VPC/private deployment supports BYOK with KMS/HSM via standard key wrapping, and we can map to your key stores. We'll need network whitelisting and an attestation exchange.
[03:12] Samir (Redwood): On the MSA timeline — legal has suggested two weeks for initial redlines, is that feasible?
[03:19] Ava (Triton): Two weeks is tight but ok if we get an initial SOW and pricing now.
[03:24] Samir (Redwood): I'll get the SOW/pilot economics over within 48 hours.
[03:29] Marcus (Triton): For the pilot, what's the recommended pilot size to validate latency and cost?
[03:35] Leah (Redwood-SE): Usually 1-2M tokens/day for 2 weeks gives us good telemetry. If you want stress testing we can do spike tests.
[03:44] Elliot (Triton): Ok. procurement flagged a concern around data residency in backups — where are snapshots stored for Private?
[03:51] Leah (Redwood-SE): With Private or VPC, snapshots live in your account/region if on cloud; for on-prem we can avoid cloud snapshots entirely. We'll document policies.
[04:03] Priya (Triton): Requesting the DPA — specifically retention, deletion APIs, and subprocessor list.
[04:10] Maya (Redwood-CSM): We'll share a DPA template and subprocessor list. note some names may be redacted for partner confidentiality, but core infra partners are listed.
[04:20] Ava (Triton): Also need to understand SLA credits mechanism and how it's applied to committed vs pilot.
[04:27] Samir (Redwood): SLA credits apply differently: Dedicated has explicit uptime SLOs with credits; pilot is best-effort but we can contract minimum availability for pilot as a one-off.
[04:38] Marcus (Triton): Are there any export control or regional data transfer clauses we should watch for?
[04:45] Samir (Redwood): We have standard export control language; for EU-only deployments we can add residency language. we'll flag that for legal.
[04:54] Elliot (Triton): Who at Redwood can sign with our procurement if we get to commitments?
[04:59] Samir (Redwood): For pilot SOW AE can sign; for MSAs typically our legal counsel signs— I'll introduce them once we have redlines.
[05:07] Ava (Triton): Good. one more operational note: can you provide an example runbook for incident response and rollback?
[05:14] Leah (Redwood-SE): Yes, we have an incident runbook and rollback playbook — I'll attach a sanitized copy.
[05:22] Speaker 1 (ops): audio dropped at 05:37 for a sec — may be garbled in transcript.
[05:27] Marcus (Triton): No worries.
[05:29] [05:30] Samir (Redwood): Summarizing: we'll send pricing + SOW, security pack, and DPA template. Priya and Leah will schedule the security deep-dive. Legal teams to exchange redlines.
[05:45] Ava (Triton): For the procurement gate, the committee also wants a competitor comparison — can you include a short note comparing hosted vs doing it in-house?
[05:54] Samir (Redwood): Yes, I'll add a short competitive note — cost model, ops burden, and time-to-value.
[06:02] Priya (Triton): On SOC docs, please blur any customer-specific artifacts.
[06:07] Maya (Redwood-CSM): will do.
[06:10] Elliot (Triton): If we decide on Private, what's the lead time for a VPC deployment?
[06:15] Leah (Redwood-SE): Typical VPC onboarding is 2-3 weeks for the first environment, faster for subsequent. On-prem can be longer depending on air-gap restrictions.
[06:26] Marcus (Triton): Any E2E testing support? we'd like Redwood to run a short validation with our test harness.
[06:33] Leah (Redwood-SE): Yep. we can run a ridealong with your harness and capture P95/P99 latency and token cost.
[06:42] Ava (Triton): That would help. procurement asks for a single point estimate for monthly cost at 10M tokens/mo — best guess?
[06:50] Samir (Redwood): I'll give a range in the deck. depends on model family and quantization; I'll present low/median/high buckets.
[06:59] Priya (Triton): Legal also wanted to confirm data deletion APIs exist for both hosted and private.
[07:05] Leah (Redwood-SE): Yes deletion APIs exist; with hosted we have retention windows, with private you control the retention. we'll give API docs.
[07:13] Samir (Redwood): Any blockers to meeting the Friday procurement gate if we deliver docs tomorrow?
[07:19] Ava (Triton): No blockers, procurement will review docs and come back with questions.
[07:24] Marcus (Triton): We'll likely ask legal to push redlines same day, but their bandwidth may be limited.
[07:30] Samir (Redwood): Understood. We'll mark target dates in the action items.
[07:36] Leah (Redwood-SE): small technical aside — if you plan to use long context (2k+ tokens) we should pick kernels optimized for that; otherwise default is tuned for 1k context.
[07:47] Elliot (Triton): noted.
[07:49] [07:50] Maya (Redwood-CSM): I'll log all action items in CRM and set reminders.
[07:56] Ava (Triton): ok that's it from us.
[07:58] Samir (Redwood): Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD with the packet.
[08:05] [END] Some background noise at 00:42 and 05:37, transcript may have small mis-attributions.
